title: seqlen-kvcache-scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad for the odd failure we hit when clients push sequences near 4k-8k boundary. Purpose: collect commands tried, reproducible snippets, kernel selection traces, hypotheses, and next steps. Not polished — notes to self.

Background/context:
- Repro: heavy prompt prefix (~3800 tokens) + 512-token user + streaming enabled. Failures seen when sequence_length_total > ~4096 on gpus with 80GB memory (A100).
- Symptoms: one of these: stalled response (no more tokens), runtime assertion in attention kernel, occasional KV cache mismatch (size/shape).
- Affected flow: hosted inference + dedicated pools; seems more frequent with model variants using rotary embeddings and qkv fused kernels.

Commands / experiments I ran (chronological):
1) basic curl reproduce (minimal):
   curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
     -H "Content-Type: application/json"
     -d '{"model":"rw-open-13b","inputs":"<long_prefix>...","max_new_tokens":512,"stream":false}' | jq .
   -> sometimes returns partial then hangs.

2) local runtime invoke (dev box) with env toggles:
   export KV_CACHE_ENABLED=1
   export ATTENTION_KERNEL_SELECT=auto   # tried auto, flash, scaled_dot
   ./rdw-local-serve --model /models/rw-open-13b --max-seq 8192 --port 8080 &
   curl -s http://localhost:8080/generate -d @payload.json | tee out.json

3) force disable KV cache:
   export KV_CACHE_ENABLED=0
   -> behavior: previously-hanging requests complete (slower) but no assertion. Strong hint KV cache plays role.

4) run unit test with seq-length boundary:
   pytest tests/test_kv_cache.py::test_append_large_prefix -k boundary -q
   output snippet:
   ==== FAILURES ===
   E AssertionError: KV cache shape mismatch at step 512
   E Expected: (1, 32, 4608, 64)  Got: (1, 32, 4480, 64)

5) kernel debug logging (increased log level):
   RDW_LOG_LEVEL=debug ./rdw-local-serve ...
   relevant lines: 
     [kernel-selector] seq_stats: median=128, p95=3072, max=4336
     [kernel-selector] selected_kernel=flash_attn_v2 fallback=scaled_dot cond=seq>2048
     [kv-manager] alloc_kv_buffer requested=4608*head_dim (bytes=...)
     [kv-manager] committed_kv_len=4480 (mismatch detected when copying prefix)
     [attention] flash_attn_v2: runtime_assert seq_len<=allocated_kv_len (4336<=4480)

6) tried increasing reserved_kv_margin in runtime config to +20%:
   config: reserved_kv_margin: 0.2
   -> reduced frequency but not fixed. Some requests still hit mismatch where committed_kv_len < expected prefix length.

Observed error snippets: (copied raw)
- "runtime_assert failed: seq_len <= kv_allocated_len at attention.cpp:421"
- "kv_copy: truncated_write: requested 4608 but wrote 4480"
- "kernel-selection: flash_attn_v2 chosen, but backend returned invalid kv stride"
- "rpc: stream terminated unexpectedly (code=13)"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Off-by-one / rounding when computing requested KV buffer in mixed-quant configs. Code path: quantized weights -> kernel-specific head_dim rounding (e.g., pad to 64) -> margin incorrectly applied before pad. Leads to under-allocation for some sequence lengths.
2) Race between async prefix cache refill and attention kernel starting: if prefix streaming appends KV while attention kernel reads expected length, a timing window could see mismatch. More likely when streaming=true + parallel KV refill threads.
3) Kernel selector heuristics pick flash_attn_v2 for sequences > 2048 but flash_attn has stricter alignment expectations; fallback path not fully ensuring buffer layout compatibility.
4) Memory fragmentation on long-running processes causing committed_kv_len returned by allocator to be slightly smaller than request (we assume allocator always satisfies or throws).

Quick notes from code inspection: (file paths adapted)
- kv_manager::reserve(length) returns RoundedUpLength = round_up(length, kv_pad) where kv_pad depends on kernel. But in kv_cache.cpp we do apply reserved_margin BEFORE rounding: final_alloc = round_up(request * (1+margin), kv_pad) ; the callers sometimes pass head_dim product already rounded -> double rounding mismatch.
- kernel_selector::choose() has heuristics: if median_seq > threshold AND max_seq < limit choose flash_attn; but we base median on sample window that may not include current request's extreme prefix; could mis-classify.

Mini experiment matrix (notes):
- KV_CACHE=1, kernel=auto, margin=0.0 -> fail ~65% for seq_total>4096
- KV_CACHE=1, kernel=scaled_dot -> success ~95% (slower)
- KV_CACHE=0 -> success (expected slower, no KV)
- KV_CACHE=1, kernel=flash_attn_v2, margin=0.2 -> success ~90% but occasional mismatch (rare)

Repro script idea:
- generate prefix with random token lengths to push total into [4000,4600]
- do 50 sequential requests with same websocket / keep-alive, streaming on 
- enable RDW_LOG_LEVEL=debug and save logs

Short-term mitigations shipped to canary (notes):
- Increase default reserved_kv_margin to 0.25 for flash_attn variants (rolled to canary cluster on 2026-02-18).
- Add assert + fallback: if kv_copy wrote fewer tokens than expected, immediately abort kernel and retry with scaled_dot (non-fused) kernel. (PR: linked above).

Open action items / next steps:
- [ ] Write a focused unit test that simulates mixed-padding rounding behavior; trigger reserve+roundup logic for head_dim variants 32/64/128.
- [ ] Add stronger telemetry: record requested_kv_len vs allocated_kv_len + kernel chosen per request in traces (trace fields: requested_kv_len, allocated_kv_len, kernel).
- [ ] Investigate possible race in streaming prefix path: instrument lock stats on KV append and kernel start.
- [ ] Run stress job on dedicated canary with 24h of mixed-length traffic (script above) and capture >5000 requests.
- [ ] Check allocator implementation for silent truncation: ensure allocator either returns bigger buffer or errors.

Notes to self:
- Talk with Diego about the allocator (he mentioned a vendor patch earlier).
- Priya to review kernel padding behavior across quantized kernels (128/64 head dims).

Random logs / useful hashes: 
- Sample failing request id: req_20260302_7f9a3b (attached in canary logs)
- Stack trace snippet: 
   #0 attention::compute() at attention.cpp:421
   #1 model::forward() at model.cpp:1102
   #2 rpc::handle_request() at rpc_server.cpp:287

Questions / unknowns: 
- Is our KV buffer accounting done per-request or per-shard? (I thought per-request, but observed values suggest shared buffer in some code paths).
- Does flash_attn_v2 require alignment to 128 bytes per head stripe? Need to confirm with kernel docs.

If I were to summarize in one line: "KV under-allocation (rounding + margin + kernel alignment) causes attention kernels to read more tokens than backed memory, triggering truncation/assertions; fallback fixes but we should address allocation logic."

If someone lands on this doc: please add reproduce logs, link the canary request id, and mark items completed.

-- Maya
